chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: A new week began with a package from the city museum. Ada arrived before the children and helped Nia open the box. Inside was a round ball, a small battery lamp, and a paper sign showing the shape of the moon on different nights. A museum worker had written that the materials were free to borrow, except the battery must not be left in the lamp when it was stored. Nia made a new label for the box.
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: raw what they noticed. Arun set the museum box on a high shelf and kept the battery in a separate bag. When the last child left, Nia looked at the two drawings on the table. One showed a bright full moon; the other showed a small curve. Both had come from one ball and one light. She began to see why simple models were powerful: they let people test an idea with their own hands.

chapterReports.title: 走錯的時鐘
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: Nia believed the next lesson would be easy. She wanted to teach the class how the sky changed from day to night. She brought two clocks, one for the wall and one for her desk. As the children entered, the wall clock showed five, although it was just after ten in the morning. Finn laughed and said the clock wanted to dream about dinner. Nia laughed too, then noticed that the second clock was also w
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: he also wrote something else: a lesson was not ruined when an error appeared. The error could become a question. The stick in the yard had shown one kind of change; the clock on the wall had shown another. People could use both, as long as they knew what each one could and could not tell them. She closed the room, feeling less afraid of making mistakes in front of her students.

chapterReports.title: 日落後的公園
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The class planned a short evening visit to the city park. This would be their first chance to see a few real stars together. Nia wrote a note to every family: children must come with an adult, and nobody should walk away from the group. The park officer showed her a flat place near a bench, away from baseball games and the road. "People come here to walk after dinner," he said. "Please leave the p
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: Bo said the fence noise had frightened him. Ada wrote the answers without changing them. There was no prize for seeing the most stars. The group had gone outside, used their eyes, stayed together, and returned safely. That was enough for a first evening. Nia went home thinking that the best star lesson might be about the people standing under the sky as much as the sky itself.

chapterReports.title: 湖邊的一個故事
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The next Saturday was the town's spring festival, so the center room was busy. People carried rice, fruit, and hot dishes along Red Brick Street. A grandmother called Mrs. Noor visited the class with a card showing a lake under the moon. She said she had lived beside that lake when she was young. "My family watched the moon there every year," she said. "It was a small joy in a hard life." Nia aske
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: sked Mrs. Noor for permission to keep the card on the wall for the six weeks. Mrs. Noor agreed. "I'm sure other families have stories too," she said. Nia wrote a new idea: invite one visitor each week to share a memory, then choose one part to test or explain. It would be a gentle way to connect everyday life with science. She could already see a new kind of class taking shape.

chapterReports.title: 每雙手都能讀的地圖
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: A new student came to the center with his brother. His name was Tomas, and he was blind. He knew the street well because he walked it with a white cane. He asked Nia if the star class was only for people who could see pictures. Nia was quiet for half a minute. She had made every activity with drawings. "I don't know the best way yet," she said, "but I want to work with you." Tomas smiled. "Then as
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: wded string and one with clear spaces. "We need both," she told Ada. "The first shows why we changed the second." Ada agreed. A class record was not only a place for finished work. It should also show how people learned. Nia looked again at the six-week plan. The next month would be busy, but the room now had one more person who could help decide what the lessons should become.

chapterReports.title: 突然變冷的教室
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On a cold Tuesday, the weather changed quickly. Nia drove past the center in her brother's car and saw a blue sign on the door: The heating fan was not working. Arun had already called the repair service, but the worker could not come until afternoon. The room would be safe later, but it was too cold for the morning group. Nia wanted to call every family before they left home. She did not have eve
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: the service note and the date of the check. "Good," she said. She did not want to guess about safety. At home she made a simple plan for cold days: contact families, offer an indoor backup room, and write down the change. She had begun the six weeks thinking only about the stars. Now she understood that keeping a class open meant looking after much more than the lesson itself.

chapterReports.title: 我們在太空中的位置
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The center reopened, and Nia set a large picture of the solar system on the wall. Ada rode her bicycle to the library to borrow a second book. When she returned, she found Finn and Tomas looking at a model of Earth. Tomas said, "I can feel the raised land on this ball, but where does our town belong?" Nia placed a small soft dot on the model and said it stood for their home. "The planet is much bi
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: y did not know. Ada packed the paper maps in a box and took the borrowed book back to the library. She told Nia that the class was growing more careful. "At first, they wanted the biggest light," she said. "Now they ask whether the light is right for the question." Nia was glad. Learning science was becoming less about being amazed and more about finding a way to ask and check.

chapterReports.title: 誰能使用這間教室
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On Monday, Mr. Hale told Nia that a city hotel had asked to use the center room on Saturdays. The hotel could pay more money than the star class. Nia felt worried. The room was small, but it had become important to everyone who came. "Is there a rule about who gets the space?" she asked. Mr. Hale said the city had a public-use rule: a new business could not simply take a room that people were alre
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: and the changes made for safety. She left an empty space for tomorrow's questions. The plan did not promise that every night would be clear or every child would see a star. It promised honest lessons, open questions, and careful use of a shared room. Nia looked at the pages and felt a little more ready. Whatever the board decided, she could speak about work she had truly done.

chapterReports.title: 牆上的名字
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: Nia's aunt Celia came to visit with a box of fresh lemons from her garden. She had owned a small business for many years and knew that a kind offer could still bring a hard question. "Have you already agreed to put a donor's name on the wall?" she asked. Nia said no. A woman had offered a clock, but they had chosen paper instead. Celia smiled. "Good. First ask what the class needs. Then ask what t
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: . "Then you are growing into the work." Nia did not feel like a great teacher yet. She still needed help with costs, weather, and difficult questions. But she had made choices she could explain. The sign on the door did not have a rich person's name in large letters. It said, in clear blue print: Star Class—All Questions Welcome. That was the name the group had chosen together.

chapterReports.title: 市場裡的問題
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: Nia returned to the weekend market to invite more visitors to the star class. Mara's sister had a small restaurant there, and she offered them a table near the door. The place was full of food smells. A woman in a wide hat asked whether the class was expensive. Nia said no; the center paid for the room and the activities were free. "Then how can you keep it open?" the woman asked. Nia showed her t
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: d. "We only want the people who come to have a good place to learn." Ada counted the papers that had been taken, but she did not count them as students. "A paper is not a person," she said. "We will know who comes when they arrive." Nia wrote that line in the class notes. The day had not brought a room full of new learners, but it had given her a better way to explain the work.

chapterReports.title: 螢幕上的承諾
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: A new problem appeared on Wednesday. Someone had posted a message online saying the star class would show a hundred falling stars on Saturday. Nia knew that was not correct. She was angry, not because the picture was ugly, but because families might come expecting something she could not give. Ada found that the post had started with a local writer who had misunderstood a short note about a possib
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: m or give him a reward. He showed the corrected message and said he would check his sources next time. Nia thanked him for being clear. She had been worried that the mistake would hurt the class. Instead, the group had learned to ask a simple but important question: How do we know this is true? Nia put that question at the top of the board, where every new student could see it.

chapterReports.title: 一次問一個問題
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: As the trial went on, the center room felt busy. Some people wanted more pictures, while others asked for more time to talk. Nia had to decide what was enough for one lesson. She asked each person to write one question on a card. A driver who had come after a long shift asked whether city air could hide stars. A married couple asked if the moon changed shape because of clouds. Finn wanted to repea
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: er a note: You do not have to answer everything to have taught something. Nia read it twice. She had spent much of the week afraid of disappointing people. Now she saw that an honest "not yet" could be useful. On Saturday, the group had learned to organize questions, listen to each other, and choose a next step. That work was real, even without a dramatic view of the night sky.

chapterReports.title: 草地上的練習
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On a clear morning, Mr. Hale offered the star class a chance to use a flat grass field behind the center for an evening lesson. Nia was certain it would be helpful if the weather stayed clear. She went there with Finn's father, Ada, and the center's safety leader. They checked the ground before inviting any child. One corner had a giant hole left by old garden work, so they set the observing area
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: e by touch. Bo marked the hole with a big circle. Finn marked the light near the bathroom path. The map was not a picture of stars, yet everyone could see why it mattered. "We want an open sky," Nia said, "but first we need an open, safe place to stand." The children nodded. She placed the map beside the star cards. Both were now part of learning to look carefully at the world.

chapterReports.title: 門口的訪問
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: A young newspaper writer came to interview Nia about the star class. He had heard that another group might take over the room. Nia told him that the city had not decided yet. "Please do not write that we have lost the room," she said. "That would mean something different from what is true." The writer nodded. A black dog lay on the ground near the center door, looking at people with one bright eye
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: bout the program, but it could not make the decision for the board. She asked Finn what he thought the class should do next. He said they should finish the six weeks and show the board what everyone had learned. Nia agreed. The idea was small and steady. She did not need the newspaper to call her a hero. She wanted the facts about the room, the people, and the work to be clear.

chapterReports.title: 留在室內的那一夜
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The weather report showed strong rain for Saturday. Nia had planned an evening sky visit, but she changed it to an indoor lesson. A family had come from abroad that month and asked whether they could still join. Nia said yes and sent a short note about the change. When the rain began, water ran below the front windows, but it did not enter the room. Ada checked the door with Arun. "We don't need t
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: ndred or try to make it sound larger. A father said that the real number mattered because it showed people had chosen to come. Nia agreed. The rain was still falling hard outside, but everyone left with a clear plan and a safe way home. She stayed to clean the tables and pack the machine with Arun. It had been a night without real stars, but it was not a night without learning.

chapterReports.title: 適合每個人的光
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The final week was busy from its first morning. Nia needed to prepare the last class and a simple show of student work for the center board. She did not want a grand party. She wanted people to see what the students had made and learned. Ada carried a ball, a paper airplane, and three different types of small light into the room. The airplane was for a lesson about how far a thing could travel; it
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: Ada said it sounded simple enough for anyone to understand. Nia thought of the early mornings, the bad weather, and the many small changes they had made. None of that work was as beautiful as a large picture of the stars. But it was the reason the children could come back each week and feel welcome. She switched off the last lamp and left the room ready for the final Saturday.

chapterReports.title: 大家都能使用的話
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The final practice session began on Thursday with a question from a new visitor: "What grade do I need to be in to join?" Nia smiled. "No grade is needed," she said. "A baby may sit with a parent, and an older person may ask a new question." The visitor pointed to the paper models and asked why they were so simple. Nia invited him to sit on a bench near the door while she explained. The models wer
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: wrote the four words on a board near the door. The class had not learned everything about space. No one could in six weeks. But they had learned how to look, ask, test, and listen. They were ready to show the center board what had happened in the little room. Nia asked everyone to check the floor for paper before leaving. They went home with their work safe and the room clean.

chapterReports.title: 我們可以使用的地方
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On Friday, Nia went to the center office to finish the class report. Arun greeted her with a cheerful "Hello!" and offered her a chair. The report had pages of notes, but Nia wanted the board to understand what each page meant. She put the oldest work at the bottom of the pile and the newest on top. She did not want to hide the mistakes. "This may look a little crazy," she said, "but the changes a
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: a few sheets of paper. The report was not a prize. It was a way to tell the truth about six weeks. She closed the folder and put it near her door. On Monday she would bring it to the meeting. For the first time, she was not planning a long speech to make everyone like her. She was planning to answer questions about the work, with the students' choices still visible on the page.

chapterReports.title: 試辦期的最後一夜
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The morning was rainy, and Nia thought the final outdoor visit might be lost. But the weather report showed a chance of clear sky after dinner. She called the center officer on her cellphone and asked whether the grass field had passed its safety check. He said the hole had been blocked, the path light fixed, and the work recorded. Nia asked for a copy of the check before inviting families. She al
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: the field, with people standing far apart under three stars. She thanked him and asked if she could keep it with the class work. He agreed. The trial was now finished, but there was still a meeting to come. Nia looked out at the clear patch of sky. She felt glad, not because the stars had followed her plan, but because the class had learned what to do even when the sky did not.

chapterReports.title: 教室繼續開放
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On Monday morning, Nia carried the class report to the center board. She passed a busy street that led toward the airport and heard a noisy truck stop near a market sale. A man pushed a dirty cart away from the road while a child tried to catch a rolling orange. Nia helped the child stop safely and then continued walking. She was not late, but she felt lucky to have a few extra minutes. She had sp
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: prepare a new moon map?" he asked. "Yes," Nia said. "And you can choose what to show next time." At the center, the little paper stars were still on the wall. They were not real stars, but they marked the place where real questions had begun. Nia opened her notebook and wrote the date of the next class. The end of six weeks had become the beginning of something that could last.

chapterReports.title: 空掉的綠色架子
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: At seven a.m., Ivy came early to the school garden. The sun was just above the roof. She ate fruit and a small cake for breakfast, then looked at the green shelf near the door. Yesterday, a heavy green box had stood there. It held seeds, signs, and a little book for the garden club. Now the shelf was empty. The bell rang for the first class, but Ivy did not move. Their garden day was only four wee
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: ry” could be read. Ivy put the paper between two clean pages without trying to pull it apart. Jun wanted to ask every student in the school, but Ms. Wen suggested a smaller first step. They would speak to the people who used the garden yesterday. Ivy closed her book. She still wanted the green box back, yet she also wanted everyone to feel safe when they answered her questions.

chapterReports.title: 輪子的痕跡
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The next morning was sunny. Ivy's cousin Leo came to school for a family visit and brought a small science tool that could measure the weather. He was also good at drawing maps. He saw two wheel marks in the soft earth near the gate. “A cart may have passed here,” he said. Jun wanted to follow the marks at once, but Ivy asked Ms. Wen first. The marks might belong to a cart carrying food, not to th
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: room. The other went toward the water station and the old park. She had never been there with the club. Mr. Reed offered to show the way on Thursday, when the station was open to school groups. “That will be safer,” Ivy said. Jun put away the map and helped carry the empty food bags. He was learning that being useful did not always mean being the first person to run somewhere.

chapterReports.title: 水邊的道路
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On Thursday the club walked with Ms. Wen and Mr. Reed to the water station. The road followed the river for a short way. Far away, beyond a low bridge, they could see the beach. A bird sat on the bridge rail. Jun wondered whether the wide wheel marks could still be found, but the rain had washed the road clean. Ivy asked everyone to stay on the safe side of the road. They were there to learn what
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: alone could lead them to the box. Then Mr. Reed showed her the garden gate. A new sign had appeared there: “Work area. Keep clear.” It had not been there last week. Someone was making repairs near the garden, and the work had started before the box went missing. Ivy copied the sign into her notes. At last they had a question about the place itself, not just a mark on the road.

chapterReports.title: 施工區域
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: A cool wind began to blow across the school yard. A cloud covered the morning sun. Near the garden, two workers from a small factory were setting square stones beside a new water pipe. One tall worker lifted a cheap plastic cover from a pile of tools. Ivy stood behind the safety line with Ms. Wen. She did not step into the work area. A butterfly flew past the stones, and a little boy ran after it.
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: new list: the box was on the shelf before the repair; a worker moved garden things inside; and the school had several storage rooms. Ivy asked Jun to draw a plan of the rooms from the school map. A drop of water fell from his wet hair onto the page, and he shook his head with a laugh. “Even the weather wants to add a mark,” he said. They agreed to ask before entering any room.

chapterReports.title: 種子需要時間
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On Monday Ms. Wen took the club to the garden without the green box. “We can still learn,” she said. The children put bean seeds from a class bag into small cups. They used a tool to dig little holes, then covered the seeds with earth. A frog sat near the water bowl, watching them. A hen from the school farm walked by with her neck held high. Jun wanted to race the others and finish first, but Ivy
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: Ivy chose the boy who had dropped his cup, because he wanted a chance to show what he could do. He walked slowly and kept both hands under the tray. No cup fell. Ivy thanked him, and he looked proud. On the way home she remembered that finding the green box mattered, but how they treated one another during the search mattered too. Both things were part of making a good garden.

chapterReports.title: 好多箱子的屋子
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On the weekend, Ivy went with her mother to her uncle Dan's house. He lived near the river and had a small boat, which he used only when the weather was good. Before they arrived, he put his coffee away from a table of tools. “Finally, my favorite visitors,” he said, waving from the door. Ivy smiled but told him about the terrible feeling of seeing the empty green shelf. Her uncle listened without
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: t forgotten the garden problem. Ivy said that was fine. A club could not ask friends to work all the time. She told him about the drawing and asked whether he could check the monkey's exact color. “Orange ears and one white tooth,” Jun said at once. Ivy wrote the answer. On Monday they would bring the picture to Ms. Wen and ask which storage rooms were safe for adults to check.

chapterReports.title: 時鐘上的錯誤
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On Monday Ms. Wen took Ivy and Jun to the school office. A clock above the door was six minutes slow. The secretary laughed when Jun pointed this out. “That small error made our meeting book look strange last week,” she said. Ivy could hear voices from the yard outside. She closed the door gently so they could listen. She had dreamed of finding the green box that day, but she knew a dream was not
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: in the yard. The sky was clear, and a thin cloud crossed the sun. Jun said he liked solving things with his hands; he did not like waiting. Ivy understood him. She also wanted to open every door and look behind every shelf. But waiting for permission was part of caring for their school. “Tomorrow we can do more,” she said. They left the locked music room alone and walked home.

chapterReports.title: 公園裡的桌子
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The music teacher found no green box in her closet. Then she told Ms. Wen about a park event held on the same day as the rain. A group had borrowed tables from school. Ivy and Jun went to the park with their teacher. Outside the gate, a girl in a bright dress was practicing a dance. Behind her, children played baseball on a field. A ball flew over the grass, and Jun moved back before it could hit
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: a park bench. It showed a drawing of three little leaves. “It might be from a school garden,” she said. Ivy asked to see the card, then compared it with Jun's drawings. The leaves looked familiar, but the writing was not theirs. It belonged to another school nearby. “We found the owner of one lost thing,” Ivy said. “That is still good.” The leader thanked her for being careful.

chapterReports.title: 奶奶的卡片
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The town held a spring festival beside the lake. Ivy visited with her grandmother, who loved to cook rice and tell stories about her long life. Grandmother brought an old garden card from home. On the back was a street name Ivy did not know. “Our town had a garden group before your school had one,” she explained. Ivy looked at the card and felt a little joy. Perhaps an older group could help them
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: ide. The teacher said the guide could help them plan a second set of seeds if necessary. “You have found something useful, even if it is not the box,” she said. Ivy felt more sure of their next step. She would ask the town garden group about safe seed storage, while Jun and Ms. Wen continued checking school rooms. They had two small jobs instead of one giant, impossible search.

chapterReports.title: 每個人都能走進的花園
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: At school Ivy met a student named Kai. He was blind and used a long cane to find his way. His older brother walked beside him, but Kai chose where to go. The garden path ran between two low beds of plants, and a ball from the nearby sports field sometimes hit the fence. Kai asked if there could be a clear way through the garden without anything under his feet. Ivy had been thinking about seeds; sh
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: d they did not know yet. Their teacher would check the plan and speak with the school office. Kai nodded. “Please tell me what you decide,” he said. “It is my school too.” Ivy wrote down his words. The garden was no longer only a place where seeds might grow. It was a place where the choices of different people had to fit together, just like the roots of plants under the earth.

chapterReports.title: 辦公室的清單
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The school secretary called Ivy after class. She had found a blue folder with a list of things moved during the repair. The weather had been cold and wet that morning. A small car had taken music chairs to the town center, while a larger van had carried garden tools. The secretary was not sure whether the green box was in either car. “Maybe the names of the drivers will help,” she said. Ivy thanke
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: old leaf fell near her shoe. She thought of the box and all the places it might have gone. Then she thought of Kai's words about the path. One problem had led them to see another. It was possible to care about both without solving either one that day. She wrote the next job on a new page: ask the driver to check the picture, and ask the school where the garden van had stopped.

chapterReports.title: 風與標示牌
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: A strong wind arrived before lunch. Ivy and Jun rode their bicycles to school, but walked the bikes through the busy gate. In the garden, paper labels flew off several seed cups. A girl in jeans picked them up and gave them to Ivy with a little bow. “These are not mine,” the girl said. Ivy thanked her. The writing was in two languages because children from different homes had helped make the label
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: Ivy placed the cups in a safe room and checked them a second time. She had wanted the work to be fast, but careful hands mattered more. Jun helped tie a string around the trays so they would not move on the table. They left room between the cups for air. Ivy looked at the small green leaves and smiled. The club still had a story to finish, and tomorrow might bring a new answer.

chapterReports.title: 鎮上花園的門
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The school arranged a visit to the city garden center. A small gate stood beside a low wall. Outside it, a long rope showed where visitors could stand while workers moved heavy bags of soil. Ivy and Jun followed the rule. They saw a sign asking people to borrow tools only after writing their names. A worker said the garden had used that rule for years. “Our system is not difficult,” she said, “but
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: rrowing rules could save trouble. Ivy said she had learned to ask for help without entering places that were not open to them. A boy said he wanted to make the school's garden as welcoming as this one. The worker smiled. She gave them a guide to small plants that could grow in the city. “Come again tomorrow if your teacher makes a new visit,” she said. “Good gardens take time.”

chapterReports.title: 一起訂下的計畫
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: Ms. Wen met with several parents and school workers to make an agreement about the garden. Ivy's aunt came as one of the family visitors. She wore gloves and a blue uniform because she worked at the town garden center. “Can children help paint the new signs?” she asked. The principal said yes, as long as an adult watched the tools and the paint was safe. Ivy was happy. It was the first time the sc
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: work next week. Ivy said she could help, but she did not want to make every decision herself. Kai should have a say about the path, Jun about the signs, and the younger children about the plants they wanted to learn from. The principal agreed. For the first time, Ivy felt like a real leader. She was not the boss of her friends. She was the person making room for them to speak.

chapterReports.title: 市場大廳
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The school arranged a visit to the market hall. At the front door, Ivy saw a store selling hats and T-shirts. A visitor was eating a meal at a small restaurant nearby. Beside the door a worker was fixing a pipe, and water had made the ground wet. Ms. Wen asked the children to walk around the work area. “Please stay with us,” she said. Jun looked at the signs and said the market felt like a world o
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: st while Ms. Wen counted the group. Jun said they had come close to an answer. Ivy said the green container might still be a different box. It would be wrong to tell the younger students that the seeds had been found. They waited for Sara to check its drawing. “I want us to be glad when we know, not only when we hope,” Ivy said. Jun agreed and offered to carry her water bottle.

chapterReports.title: 花園裡炎熱的一天
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The next day was very hot. Air above the school garden felt still, and Ivy could see heat rise from the road. The children wore hats and worked slowly. Ms. Wen told them that the garden was part of the earth and needed care in different weather. A writer from the school paper came to ask about the missing green box. Ivy said she did not know where it was, but she knew people were helping. The writ
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: hought of the children who had made the seed labels. Some had written in English, others in the language they used at home. She wished each child could see the work again. She could not know what was under the cloth until someone checked. She made a cup of water for herself, put her book away, and went to bed. Tomorrow would come soon enough without her staying awake all night.

chapterReports.title: 橘耳朵的猴子
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The next afternoon Sara called again. Two workers had moved the shelf, and she could finally see the green box. There was a monkey on its side, with orange ears and one white tooth. Ivy's face grew warm. “That really sounds like ours,” she said. Ms. Wen asked Sara to check the school name on the bottom before they made a final decision. Jun stood close enough to hear but did not shout. He was stro
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: d written on the day the box disappeared. Then she turned to the new page and wrote the answer in a careful sentence. She added the names of the people who had helped, from the garden worker to Sara at the market. She did not say that she alone had solved the problem. That would not be true. She knew the real story was made from many small pieces, held together by patient talk.

chapterReports.title: 還能長出什麼？
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The green box returned on Tuesday. Mr. Reed and another school worker opened it in a safe room, with Ivy's team watching from the door. The paper labels were dry, but one small bag of seeds had become wet. The workers placed it aside for a careful check. Yesterday the children had wanted to touch everything; today they waited. Ms. Wen said they did not need to open every bag at once. They could se
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: would help wet seeds. Mr. Reed said it would help clean the work area, but seeds needed a different kind of care. Kai asked when the firm path would be ready. The teacher said the workers had measured it today. Ivy felt that their garden was becoming more real. It was no longer only a picture on paper. The work was open for everyone to see, and the plan had room for questions.

chapterReports.title: 小徑旁的蜜蜂
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: Another problem appeared the next morning. A bee flew near the garden gate, and a child cried that it would attack everyone. A black dog behind the fence began to bark. The noise made more children run. Ivy did not move toward the bee. She asked the group to walk quietly to a clear space and find a teacher. A bee could bite or sting if it felt in danger, so they should not hit it or wave at it. Mr
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: not draw a monster with giant teeth. She drew a small animal doing what it normally did. Under the picture she wrote that people and bees needed space. Her father looked at it and smiled. “You have had many new problems this year,” he said. Ivy answered that she had also met many people ready to help. She was learning to count both the problems and the good things around them.

chapterReports.title: 太低的水管
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: Rain came again on Wednesday. The school garden's water pipe made a hard sound, and very little water came from the tap. A machine below the path had stopped working. Ivy felt hope fall for a moment. She had thought the missing box was their biggest problem. Now even the new plants might go without water. A worker asked everyone to move to the front of the garden, away from the broken pipe. Ivy ob
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: n needed. One student said a place to put shoes when they became muddy. Another said a small cover for the seed cards. Ivy wrote down their ideas. They would not do every job before the opening, and that was all right. She looked at the broken pipe below the path, then at the growing green leaves above it. The garden had problems, but it had people who knew how to ask for help.

chapterReports.title: 一步一步的小徑
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The workers finished the main garden path while the children were in class. Ivy came out and saw a light gray surface from the gate to the first flower bed. Kai arrived with his cane and asked whether he could try it. Ms. Wen said yes. His brother stood near the door, but Kai wanted to walk the way on his own. He moved slowly and stopped at the first turn. “There is a little edge here,” he said. T
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: kitchen made her hungry again. She told her mother how Kai had tried the new path. “Did it work?” her mother asked. “Mostly,” Ivy said. “There is still one edge to fix.” She was glad she could give an answer that was both hopeful and true. The garden would open soon, but being ready did not mean that nobody could find a problem. It meant that someone would listen when they did.

chapterReports.title: 正式開放前的測試
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The club held a small test day for children from a younger grade. A baby plant stood in a dry pot near the gate. A bench gave visitors a place to rest. Ivy asked the children not to climb on the low garden wall, because the wet earth beside it could be soft. A boy carried a plate of small snacks, while a girl read plant names aloud. The teacher watched from near the path. They wanted to find any w
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: the path, stopped near the flowers, and said he could find the sign easily. Ms. Wen asked whether anything else should change. Kai said the bench could move one step away from the turn. The workers agreed. Ivy looked at the new path, the plants, and the little notes on her page. Their garden was becoming ready because different people had told the truth about what they needed.

chapterReports.title: 每個箱子都有位置
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The school office held a short meeting about keeping things safe. Ms. Wen said the green box belonged to the garden club, but the school still needed a clear place for it. “Hello, everyone,” said the secretary as people came into the room. She put the box on a low table and showed its name on the bottom. A worker brought a new label and a small shelf. “Which room should this go in?” he asked. Ivy
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: window. The green box sat dry on its new shelf. She never wanted to find it lost again, but she also knew accidents could happen. The important part was having a way to notice, ask, and correct a mistake. She looked at Jun and said, “This is a better home for our box.” “Yes,” he answered. The monkey with orange ears smiled from the shelf, ready for the next group of gardeners.

chapterReports.title: 開放前的雨
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: On the day before the opening, rainy weather came across the town. Wind pushed water along the school road, and everyone moved away from the garden's low beds. Ivy checked the date on her cellphone. The garden day was tomorrow. She had hoped to finish every sign, yet the last one was still wet. Ms. Wen invited the club to meet in the school kitchen, where the tables were clean and dry. They would
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: eet at school in the morning, whatever the weather. She did not ask anyone to come early without permission or to carry heavy things. The garden could wait for safe hands. At home her mother showed her the small plant growing on the kitchen window. Its leaves were new and green. Ivy smiled. She had spent weeks learning that life could keep moving, even when plans had to change.

chapterReports.title: 花園開門的日子
chapterReports.sceneOpeningEn: The rain stopped in the morning. Ivy could see the school garden from the gate, and the sight made her smile. Its new path was clean, the green box was safe, and small leaves had begun to grow in every bed. Jun had cut paper signs the night before, and they looked bright against the wet earth. A worker pushed a cart of chairs to the side, away from the path. “Now we are ready,” Ms. Wen said. Ivy f
chapterReports.sceneClosingEn: The monkey with orange ears faced the room. Ivy remembered the day she had first seen the empty shelf. She had felt that everything was lost. Now she knew how many small good things could grow from a hard question. “Shall we come back tomorrow?” Jun asked. Ivy smiled. “Yes. Plants need care after the party too.” Together they closed the door and went home under the evening sun.

after.zh: 一隻小蟲沿著廳堂空白的牆面慢慢爬行。塞拉想，也許這個角落能成為需要休息的鄰居暫時避開喧鬧的地方。

after.zh: 一隻小蟲鑽進裂縫。妮亞蹲下來仔細查看，發現裂縫比想像中更寬。她擔心木板正在裂開，便從袋子裡拿出相機，拍下損壞的地方。

before.zh: 泰絲原以為可以找到整支隊伍，結果只遇到一個人。她帶著較小的希望回家，但那份希望是真實的。

after.en: Tess had arrived with only her own name on the list. Now Ben had written the next meeting time, and June was still smiling by the door. They did not have seven players yet, but she no longer had to make the plan alone.
after.zh: 泰絲來時，名單上只有她自己的名字。如今班已寫下下次集合時間，瓊還在門邊微笑。他們還湊不滿七位球員，但她終於不必獨自籌畫了。

before.zh: 一隻小蟲爬過窗戶。她打開窗戶聽，卻聽不見鳥叫聲。

after.en: A small bug crept along the cold window. Tavi wondered why it had appeared so early. She opened the window and listened for the birds that usually returned before spring, but heard none.
after.zh: 一隻小蟲沿著冰冷的窗戶緩緩爬行。塔薇不明白牠為何這麼早就出現。她打開窗戶，想聽聽通常在春天前回來的鳥兒，卻一聲鳥鳴也沒聽見。

after.zh: 早上七點，妮雅站在紅磚街的公寓外，沉重的教學袋放在早餐桌旁。距離第一堂課還有充裕的時間。
